title: Lease-ring KV cohort rebalancer and block-lease interface for hot-slice pinning
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Production traces showed repeated churn on a small set of hot prefix blocks when continuous-batching workloads interleave long and short sequences. Eviction thrashing increases 95p latency and wastes kernel hot pages. This PR introduces a lightweight block-lease abstraction and a lease-ring cohort rebalancer to reduce premature evictions for hot slices. Design and scope: 1) block-lease: a short-duration, non-exclusive lease that a requester can acquire for a block to prevent evaporation during retry/batching windows. Leases are cheap metadata only and time out automatically; explicit release paths added for fast-paths. 2) lease-ring cohort rebalancer: a compact ring index that groups blocks into moving cohorts by recent-hit buckets and uses a low-cost sampler to bias reuse decisions toward cohort members. The rebalancer nudges eviction scores rather than hard-pinning, which keeps memory pressure responsive. 3) hot-slice tier: an ephemeral pinning tier for slices that are repeatedly accessed within a lease window; slices here are cheaper to keep resident and get priority during continuous batching merges. 4) scheduler and kernel hints: when a lease is held, the local scheduler attempts co-located batch placement and prefers kernels with fused attention and kv-prefetch paths; a kernel hint API was extended for backends to expose coalesced-page preference. 5) observability and flags: per-cohort hit-rate, lease-acquire latency, eviction-deferred counters and a feature flag redwood.runtime.lease_ring.enabled to gate rollout. Implementation notes: changes are additive and guarded behind the feature flag. BlockManager gained TryAcquireLease/ReleaseLease and a lease bookkeeping ring with O(1) amortized maintenance. Eviction heuristics now include a lease_score multiplier and cohort_decay window. Integrations: continuous-batcher consults TryAcquireLease during request coalescing and will extend KV cache retention for held leases until batch commit completes. Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for lease lifecycle, deterministic rebalancer simulation tests, and end-to-end perf-canary runs using mixed short/long prompts. Canary results: 12-18% median latency improvement on chat-mixed workloads and 20-25% reduction in 95p token latency under sustained load; token cost impact measured <1.2% on our synthetic replay. Rollout plan: enable at 5% for 24h, expand to 25% for 48h, then 100% if no regressions; automated rollback if error rate or tail latency degrade beyond thresholds. Backwards compatibility: non-lease-aware backends fall back to current behavior. Migration and operational impact: minor increase in metadata allocations per node (tunable ring size, default 2048 entries). Security and debugging: new debug endpoint /admin/lease-ring/state to inspect cohort buckets and outstanding leases (guarded by internal auth).

review_comments: Marcus: Nice low-risk approach. Two nits: prefer atomic<uint32_t> for lease counters to reduce false-sharing and add a microbench for TryAcquireLease hot-path.
Asha: Addressed both nits in commit 2/6. Switched counters and added microbench; numbers attached to perf-canary config.
Diego: Question about race between lease expiry and batch commit. Can we ensure the batch will not observe a reclaimed block?

Asha: Lease guarantees are soft—when a lease expires we only lower eviction bias; continuous-batcher holds a short commit token which prevents immediate reclamation. Added comment and test to make the race deterministic in simulation.
Priya: Approve after CI green. Observability looks sufficient for initial rollout.
release_notes: Add lease-ring cohort rebalancer and block-lease interface to reduce eviction thrash for hot KV slices; guarded by feature flag redwood.runtime.lease_ring.enabled; improves median and tail latency for mixed-length batching workloads; configurable ring size and lease windows.
rollout_plan: feature flag gated; 5% for 24h -> 25% for 48h -> 100% with automated rollback on SLO regressions; ops playbook added to docs/runtime/lease_ring.md
